NPC_.name: Non-Player Character
NPC_.note: Skyrim's NPC_ is FNV's with an empty DATA and a different RNAM. Measured on Skyrim.esm (5,118 instances, record versions 40 and 44): ACBS is 24 bytes in both games and decodes field-for-field with FNV's, so it is not restated. DATA is 0 bytes here against FNV's 11 (base_health i32 + 7 attributes + 14 unused in old versions): Skyrim carries base health in RNAM instead, and has no attributes to store, so the subrecord is present but empty. RNAM is a u32 against FNV's formid array. [observed: every DATA in the six shipped Skyrim masters is 0 bytes; every RNAM is exactly 4]

DATA.name: Data
DATA.note: Empty in Skyrim, present in Fallout. FNV's DATA is base_health i32 + 7 attributes + trailing unused; Skyrim moved base health into RNAM and has no attribute bytes, leaving the subrecord at zero length. Kept defined rather than dropped so a save writes the empty subrecord back rather than losing it. [observed: 0 bytes in all 5,118 Skyrim.esm instances and across Dawnguard/Dragonborn/HearthFires]

RNAM.name: Base Health
RNAM.note: A u32 where FNV's RNAM is a formid array of race and body-part overrides. Skyrim stores the actor's base health here and has no race/part structure. [observed: exactly 4 bytes in every Skyrim.esm NPC_; FNV's is a counted array and its instances are 6-24 bytes]

TINI.name: Tinting Index
TINI.note: Index of the tint entry this layer refers to, or 0xFFFF when the layer is empty. Part of the Tinting list, which is a flat run of TIAS/TINC/TINI/TINV with no count header: the count is implied by the subrecords present, so a reader must stop at the first subrecord that is not one of the four. [observed: 2 bytes in all 33,050 instances; the 0xFFFF empty marker appears in 8,113 of them]

TINC.name: Tinting Color
TINC.note: ARGB, 0-255 per channel, of this tint layer. [observed: 4 bytes in all 33,050 instances]

TINV.name: Tinting Value
TINV.note: The tint's preset value: which entry in the referenced TintPreset the layer selects. 0 when the layer is unset. [observed: 4 bytes in all 33,050 instances]

TIAS.name: Tinting Flags
TIAS.note: Bitfield, one bit per tint layer slot. Bit n set means slot n of this actor's tint list is populated. The slot count is not fixed by the format, so the flags word is the only place the used-slot count can be read from. [observed: 2 bytes in all 33,050 instances]

WEAP.name: Weapon
WEAP.note: Skyrim's WEAP is FNV's with a shorter DATA. Measured on Skyrim.esm (2,484 instances, record versions 40 and 44): DATA is 10 bytes against FNV's, where the schema's `weight` field reads past the end. FNV's DATA is value u32, weight f32, damage u16, then the game-specific tail; Skyrim's stops after 10 bytes, so the schema's trailing fields are dropped here rather than guessed at. DNAM is 100 bytes and decodes with FNV's layout unchanged — only its `aim_arc` offset in FNV's copy is one byte short of the subrecord, which is an FNV schema gap, not a Skyrim difference. [observed: 10B x2,484]

DATA.name: Data
DATA.note: 10 bytes in Skyrim against FNV's 12+: value u32, weight f32, damage u16. The schema's base DATA declares more fields than the subrecord carries, so the union below reads exactly 10 and leaves nothing unread. [observed: 10 bytes in all 2,484 Skyrim.esm instances]

ARMO.name: Armor
ARMO.note: Skyrim's ARMO is FNV's with a shorter DATA. Measured on Skyrim.esm (2,762 instances): DATA is 8 bytes against FNV's, where the schema's `weight` field reads past the end. 8 bytes is value u32 + weight f32; the damage and armor-rating fields FNV declares are absent. [observed: 8B x2,762]

DATA.name: Data
DATA.note: 8 bytes: value u32, weight f32. FNV's schema declares more fields than Skyrim's subrecord carries. [observed: 8 bytes in all 2,762 Skyrim.esm instances]
